Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and inherited rollout evidence, then use the wake-visual and fish-control skills before proposing the single candidate. I’ll keep the candidate rationale in the required notes and only promote an evidence-backed reusable lesson.

The wake-reading skill requires a score/diagnostic-anchored comparison, and the bookshelf skill requires the same evidence before consulting its mechanism catalog. I’m now mapping the inherited candidates, notes, and visual artifacts so the eventual edit tests one interpretable mechanism.

All four sampled rollouts are finite target captures; there is no sampled failure sheet in this workspace. I’ll therefore use the fastest capture as the strong case, the lower-load guarded capture as the most informative contrast, and the reproduced parent rollout as the baseline; I’ll keep the inherited seed domain-exit failure as metric-only context rather than invent visual claims.

The evidence now satisfies the bookshelf precondition. Because the lineage has several completed iterations that preserve success but mostly revisit phase/rate/amplitude shaping, I’m consulting the mechanism shelf for a distinct observation-side primitive; the skill’s hypotheses will not override the measured fast-route versus load tradeoff.

The bookshelf changes the candidate from another scalar tweak to a two-timescale steering test: recent circular-mean bearing will set slow mean curvature, while current body-frame bearing will retain/release the high-authority posterior half-cycle. I’m recording that visual diagnosis and falsification boundary before touching the policy, as required by the wake-reading skill.

The candidate file now contains exactly one testable architecture: slow history-based route curvature plus current-bearing posterior asymmetry. I’m promoting only the prior evidence—not the unevaluated candidate—as a reusable lesson: bearing-history smoothing improved route semantics, while the independent rate-guard evidence shows that lower loads require a separate control role.

Implementation and durable guidance are complete. I’m invoking the mandated check-runner now: first the guidance-difference guard, then the lightweight Julia policy contract, then the editable-boundary check—no CFD.

The first guard exposed a workspace metadata defect: `README.md` marks the same parent twice as “copied to guidance,” so the checker sees two parents before it compares content. I’m inspecting the guard and will make the smallest metadata repair needed, then rerun all checks.

The policy contract command is blocked by the runtime, not the candidate: this shell has no `julia` executable on `PATH` (the login profile also emitted unrelated missing-SSH-path warnings). I’m checking the pinned solver/environment for an available Julia binary, then I’ll rerun the same contract check if one exists.

All mandated checks now pass. The only repair outside the requested policy/notes/guidance content was removing a duplicated parent marker from the rendered workspace README, which was necessary for the guidance guard to identify the assigned parent unambiguously. I’m doing a final file/schema audit and then handing off the unevaluated candidate for EvE’s CFD run.

Implemented exactly one Phase 2 candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) separates history-filtered route curvature from current-bearing posterior half-cycle steering.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) contains the visual diagnosis, hypothesis, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:1) now records the evidence-backed route-versus-load lesson.
- Removed a duplicate assigned-parent marker from `README.md` that prevented validation.

All mandated non-CFD checks pass: guidance semantic change, Julia policy contract/schema, and editable-boundary validation. Formal CFD was not run.
